fixes.answer: I think it starts with education that [[nurtures]] not just intelligence but character and empathy. Providing young people with genuine opportunities to take responsibility, through mentorship or community projects, helps [[cultivate]] leadership skills early. We should also reward ethical leadership rather than [[mere ambition]]. Essentially, good leaders are developed over time, not simply born.
fixes.why: 'reward' and 'developed' are plain; marked 'nurtures' and 'mere ambition'

fixes.answer: The advantages include fresh energy, innovative ideas and a willingness to challenge [[outdated conventions]]. Young leaders can be genuinely [[dynamic]]. The main disadvantage is a lack of experience, which may lead to [[impulsive]] decisions or difficulty commanding respect from older colleagues. Ideally, a young leader would be paired with experienced mentors to balance their enthusiasm with wisdom.

I largely disagree with that idea. While some people may have a natural [[charisma]] or confidence, I firmly believe leadership is a set of skills that can be learned and refined through experience. History is full of leaders who [[grew into the role]]. To claim leaders are simply born [[undermines]] the value of hard work and personal development.
fixes.why: 'development' is plain; marked 'grew into the role'
